$comment: BLESSED RECORD — §8 rule 5 of engineering/decisions/2026-07-22-structure-derived-split-patterns.md. The `components` map is RECOMPUTED from the component manifests by tools/bless-split-oracle.js and gated by checkSplitOracle in tools/check-ownership.js (build:check). A diff there is a SPLIT-BEHAVIOR CHANGE to review, not noise: run `npm run oracle:bless` only when you intend it, and justify each moved entry in the PR. The `verified` map is AUTHORED, never recomputed — it is rule 11's precondition (the record documents a verified default, it never mints one), so an ENROLLED component must name the committed deck that exercises its split and who signed the derived facts off. Blessing REFUSES to write an entry for a newly-enrolled component that has neither. The components enrolled before that precondition landed are frozen in GRANDFATHERED (tools/bless-split-oracle.js), a shrink-only backlog, not an exemption.

journey.by: #2042 (rendered at size: story, indaco, and read page by page)
journey.note: PORTRAIT ONLY, which is the whole enrollment. All three journey slides split to one `li.journey-vstage` per page (pages 6-8, 9-11, 12-14 of 15): stage band, that stage's rows with their actor dots and per-task mood faces, and BOTH legends repeated -- a page of mood faces without the mood key is unreadable. Tasks conserved 3+2+2, 2+3+1, 2+2+1 against the unsplit render; `data-section` stays 0/1/2 across each run, so each stage still resolves its own categorical token -- the attribute-driven property `timeline-list` lacks, which is why that one is placed atomic instead. BUT WHAT THAT BUYS ON THE PAGE IS SMALL, and the first wording of this note overclaimed it. Measured from computed style on the real render: all three bands paint the SAME background (a constant `--journey-stage-bg`, 81px tall) and the categorical token reaches only a 3px `border-top`. Unsplit, the three hairlines sit adjacent and read as a sequence; one stage per page leaves a single hairline with nothing to compare it against, which two independent visual reviewers each sampled and reported as 'the three bands are the same color'. The stage NAME is set large and bold in the band, so no information is lost -- the color is redundant encoding, and it is the redundancy that the split weakens. Not changed here: filling the band with the categorical color would depart from the accent-rule-on-neutral idiom `roadmap` uses for the same job, which is a design decision about the engine's visual language rather than a defect in this split. The forward pointer names the next STAGE -- 'next: Trial', 'next: Activate' -- not an actor, verified against a 4-actor deck. LANDSCAPE is untouched and must stay so: `examples/data-viz-gallery.md` renders byte-identical through the split (sha 4c1f75b0-era A/B), because the grid form carries an absolute `--col` per task into `repeat(var(--task-count), 1fr)` and a slice would draw tasks into columns that are no longer there. `journeyStageSplit` returns null without an `ol.journey-vstack`, which is what enforces that. Reshape is `paginator`: the split paginates a vertical stack and cannot narrow anything, so it must not be marked width-reducing.

pricing.by: owner ruling 2026-09-06 ("pricing is no different than compare components. we accept the splitting"); rendered at size: portrait and read page by page
pricing.note: All THREE tier counts split, one tier per page: default 3 -> cover + 3 (deck pages 3, 3.2-3.4), `two` -> cover + 2 (4, 4.2-4.3), `four` -> cover + 4 (5, 5.2-5.5). 16 pages from 7 authored slides, 0 overflow and 0 clip warnings. The component's OWN card survives on each body page and that is the point of the enrollment (ruling 1, reuse the component's styling): the featured tier keeps its `Most chosen` flag, accent border, tinted fill and accent-colored heading on its own page, verified on all three variants. Relationship `comparison` renders "Option 1 of 3 - comparing Volume discounts - Savings guarantee" and counts correctly to 2-of-2 and 4-of-4; it is what keeps a paged comparison readable as one comparison. LANDSCAPE IS UNTOUCHED and must stay so: hd and 4K render 1 page with no warning (split is gated off `wide`, lattice-emulator.js AUTOSPLIT_APPLIES), so the native 3-across row is unchanged. WHAT MAKES THE LONE CARD FILL THE MEASURE IS NOT pricing's own CSS. pricing.styles.css:50 sets an explicit `width: calc(100% / 3 - 2 * var(--sp-md) / 3)` on the tier `li` (and :38/:40 for the two/four variants), and the portrait/tall reflow at :134-149 flips flex-direction without overriding it. The generic lone-member fill in base.modifiers.css:2676 (`width: auto` on `li:only-child`, four `.lat-split-native` repetitions to outweigh box-local portrait reflows) is what beats it. That rule's own comment names pricing as the case that surfaced it -- it was written for the enrollment that was backed out on 2026-09-01 and left in place. So this enrollment needed no CSS change, and the dependency is recorded here because nothing else states it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY, stated because the render shows it: each body page's card still carries substantial dead vertical space between the feature badges and the footnote. That is the width-relative sizing problem the catalog audit measured across the whole catalog (every length is `cqi`, so a taller box grows the card and not its contents), not something the enrollment fixes. Reshape is `paginator`, not width-reducing: cover-paginate flows the component's native cards and narrows nothing. `cover-cards` would be wrong -- it transposes a wide TABLE into cards, and pricing's tiers are already cards in a top-level <ul>.

split-compare.by: owner ruling 2026-09-06 (title, first card, second card, recommendation); rendered at size: portrait and read page by page
split-compare.note: Both split-compare slides split to FOUR pages: cover (frame label, heading, context) -> one `.option` card per page -> the `.verdict` on its own CLOSING page (deck pages 3, 3.2-3.4 and 4, 4.2-4.4). 12 pages from 6 authored slides, 0 overflow and 0 clip warnings. The `.preferred` treatment survives on the second option's page in both runs. THIS ONE NEEDED A STRATEGY AND THE REASON IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- it is the first case where the generic path provably could not do the job. Enrolled on a bare `item` axis with `cover-paginate` first: the run came out with option A's INNER ROWS paginated (2 pages, 2 rows) while option B and the verdict repeated whole on both, because the transform builds `.compare-right > .options > .option` DIVS and leaves NO top-level list for `firstList` to find. That render is what `compare-options` exists for, and it is one level deeper than the refusal recorded in split-facts.js: the note said the verdict repeats because it is a sibling of `.options`, which is true, but the options had already stopped being a sliceable collection. Contrast `pricing`, enrolled the same day, which needed no strategy at all. THE VERDICT IS A SLOT, NOT TRAILING MATERIAL, and that distinction is now pinned in the tests: `carousel.test.js` CLOSES_ON_A_SLOT lists this strategy, because the negative control 'no trailing material -> no closing page' does not hold for a run whose closing page IS the component's required recommendation. The entry fails when stale. Conservation (rule 6), the one-closing-page invariant and the no-duplication check all still run for this strategy and all pass. TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY RASTERIZING, NOT BY A GATE, and both are fixed: the first cover carried an invented `split-compare-cover` class with no CSS behind it and rendered as plain small text (now the shared `coverSection` accent field, the same one cover-paginate opens with); and the relationship signal read "Options 1-2 of 4" on a two-option comparison, because `membersIn` counts the first list's `<li>`s and this page carries one option card that has a list of its own -- fixed by stamping `data-split-label`, which auto-split.js names as the remedy for exactly this shape. The trailing-beats carry was added because the rule-6 gate caught it: reading only `.verdict` dropped an author's key insight or below-note, which land as siblings AFTER `.compare-right`. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY: the closing page seats its panel high and leaves the lower half of the page empty -- the same width-relative sizing problem the catalog audit measured across the catalog, not something this enrollment addresses. LANDSCAPE IS UNTOUCHED: split is gated off `wide` (lattice-emulator.js AUTOSPLIT_APPLIES), and `readCompareOptions` returns null without a `.compare-left`/`.compare-right` pair, so any other rendered form keeps ringing.

team-profile.by: claude/team-profile-component-qjcym1 (rendered at size: portrait, indaco, and read page by page)
team-profile.note: All five compositions split to one `li.person` per page across 45 pages: the heading repeats with `(cont.)`, each page carries the person's portrait, name, role and note intact, and the forward pointer reads `continues ->`. Axis `item` derived from the rendered <ul.team-roster>, which is the authored top-level list after the component's transform rebuilds each item -- the transform retags the <li> but does not move it, so the `ul > li` axis default still resolves and no `domSelector` is needed. list-heavy rather than atomic on purpose: a lone PERSON reads exactly as authored (a name, a role, the line about what they own -- a title AND a body), unlike a lone logo-wall mark, which would assert an endorsement nobody wrote; the reasoning is recorded at the TREATMENTS entry in lib/core/split-facts.js. This split is what caught the `bio` row defect: its text block was a wrapped flex line whose note carried `min-width: 100%`, unshrinkable, and ran up to 191px past the stage's right edge on a narrow page, losing its last word. Rebuilt as a two-track grid; re-measured at zero overflow on every one of the 45 pages. A long roster that should stay ONE slide has the in-component answer instead -- the `bench` variant drops the notes and packs six up.

math.by: #2136 (rendered at size: portrait, indaco, rasterized and read page by page)
math.note:
Four structures, four verdicts, on one 8-slide deck that comes out 28 pages with nothing clipped. equation+legend (bare p3-p6 of the run, `feature` p12-p16) and step table (`derivation`) BOTH resolve through the shared cover-paginate kernel, `item` and `row` derived off the rendered DOM: the equation `

` and the table `` repeat on every body page, which is the requirement -- a legend page without its equation is unreadable. Card stack (`theorem`) and columns (`compare`) have no collection at all, so they slice by removing spans, one blockquote / one `### ` group per page, and stamp `data-split-label` so the pointer names its successor ("-> Theorem", "-> Ridge") where `membersIn` would find nothing. `stats` and `canvas` refuse BY NAME, first, before any arm runs: letting them fall out of a member count was a claim about the two committed SAMPLES rather than about the variants, and writing the stats reading as a list instead of a paragraph made `cover-paginate` claim the slide (measured: four pages, the CI panel on a cover without the estimate it qualifies). The two paginated arms also run LAST and only on a DIRECT-CHILD collection -- run first they outranked the structural arms whenever a card or a column contained a list of its own, dropping two theorem cards and duplicating a step. Conserved: 4 legend symbols, 3 table rows, 3 cards, 2 columns, against the unsplit render. NO closing page anywhere in the deck, which is correct and was not at first: `math` claims `blockquote` + `trailing-paragraph`, so `math-structures` joins MEMBER_CLAIM_STRATEGIES -- without it the hoist read all three theorem cards as one trailing run and emitted three empty pages plus a card dump.
